newsitem.title: USA: Wife of Texas separatist pleads not guilty.
newsitem.headline: Wife of Texas separatist pleads not guilty.

text.p: The wife of a Texas separatist leader who held off police last month in the mountains of west Texas pleaded not guilty Tuesday to federal fraud and conspiracy charges.
Evelyn McLaren said in a written statement to U.S. District Judge Joe Fish that she was a "Texian," not a citizen of the United States, and therefore not bound by U.S. laws.
Fish would not allow her to read the statement in open court during the arraignment, but agreed to look at it. McLaren, 50, did not have an attorney.
She and husband Rick McLaren, a leader of the separatist group known as the Republic of Texas, were charged in a 25-count federal indictment with issuing $1.8 billion in worthless financial warrants.

Prosecutors said the warrants were used by the rebel group to open bank accounts and pay off debts. The Republic of Texas, which claims to have thousands of members and is linked to anti-government militias, says Texas is an independent nation.

McLaren, who is out of jail on $20,000 bond, said a "cease-fire" agreement signed by police and her husband May 3 to end the week-long standoff at the Republic's "embassy" in the Davis Mountains certified her status as a foreign citizen.
Police said the agreement was meaningless.

More than 200 Texas state troopers, backed by helicopters, armoured personnel carriers and battering rams, were deployed in the standoff, which was sparked by the arrest of a Republic member on weapons charges.

Rick McLaren, who vowed to fight to the death throughout the siege, surrendered when police began closing in. He is currently in jail in Marfa, Texas, awaiting his day in court on federal and state charges.
